lines: Most small businesses don't have a lead problem.
They have a leak.
Someone fills in your form on a Tuesday night, and the notification sits in an inbox nobody checks until Thursday.
By then, somebody else has answered them.
So today we're going to fix that, together, in n8n.
We'll build one workflow from an empty canvas.
It catches every enquiry, writes it down, replies within a minute, and pings your phone.
If nobody has got back to the lead by the next working morning, it reminds you.
And a second, tiny workflow tells you if any of it ever breaks.
At the end, we'll run the whole thing live, with a real form, a real inbox and a real phone.
You'll need n8n, a Google account and Telegram.
I'm on a self-hosted n8n on a small server, and I'll point out the two places where that makes a difference.
Let's open the canvas.
Here's where we're heading.
Nine nodes in the main workflow, and two in the alarm.
Don't try to memorise it. We'll add them one at a time, and test each one as we go.
First, somewhere for leads to live.
In Google Sheets, create a new spreadsheet called Leads, and in the first row type eight column headers.
Received at, name, email, phone, need, source, status and replied at, in lower case with underscores, exactly as you see them here.
n8n matches on these names, so the spelling matters.

params.show: New spreadsheet Leads, eight headers in row 1

notes.html: received_at · name · email · phone · need · source · status · replied_at

lines: Back in n8n, create a new workflow and call it Lead catcher.
Click add first step, search for form, and choose on form submission.
That's n8n's own form trigger. It hosts the form for you, so you don't need a website to follow along.

params.show: New workflow Lead catcher → Add first step → On form submission

lines: Give the form a title, get a quote.
Then add four fields.
Name, as text, required.
Email, with the element type set to email, required.
Phone, as text, optional.
And what do you need, as a text area, required.
Leave respond when on form is submitted, and in the options add a completion message.
Thanks, we've got it. Check your inbox in the next minute.

params.show: Form title, four fields, completion message

notes.html: Completion message: Thanks, we've got it. Check your inbox in the next minute.

lines: Now click execute step. n8n opens the test version of the form in a new tab.
Fill it in as a test lead and submit, and back on the canvas you can see exactly what arrived.
Name, email, phone, the question under its own label, plus submitted at and form mode.
Click the pin icon to keep this test data, so you don't have to fill in the form every time you test the next step.

params.show: Execute step → fill in the test form → pin the output

notes.html: 📌 Pin data · reuse this test lead for every step

lines: Add the next node, edit fields, and rename it tidy lead.
Set the mode to manual mapping, and add seven fields, using the same names as the sheet columns.

params.show: Edit Fields, renamed Tidy lead, Manual Mapping, seven fields

lines: Name gets the name with the spaces trimmed. Open the expression editor and type dollar json dot name dot trim.
Email gets trim and to lower case, so the same person always has the same email.
Phone and need are dragged straight in from the left.
Received at is dollar now, formatted as year, month, day, hours and minutes.
Source is fixed text, quote form.
And status is fixed text, new.

params.show: The seven fields and their expressions

notes.html: phone, need ← drag from the input

lines: Make sure include other input fields is off, so only these seven go forward.
Then execute the step, and check the output on the right. Clean, consistent, and named exactly like the sheet.

params.show: Include Other Input Fields off → Execute step

lines: Next we write the lead into the sheet, and this is the first place self-hosting matters.
On n8n Cloud, you just click sign in with Google.
Self-hosted, you need your own Google OAuth app. You set it up once, and every Google node can use it.

params.show: Why self-hosted needs its own Google OAuth app

lines: In the Google Cloud console, create a project, and enable three APIs. Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Gmail.
Drive is what lets n8n list your spreadsheets by name.

params.show: New project → enable Sheets, Drive and Gmail APIs

notes.html: Enable: Google Sheets API · Google Drive API · Gmail API

lines: Then set up the OAuth consent screen as external, and add your own email as a test user.
Create an OAuth client ID of type web application.
For the authorised redirect URI, paste the OAuth redirect URL that n8n shows you in the new credential window.
It must be your real domain, not localhost.

params.show: Consent screen (External, you as test user) → OAuth client ID (Web application) → redirect URI from n8n

lines: Copy the client ID and client secret into the n8n credential, and click sign in with Google.
One warning before we move on. While your consent screen is in testing mode, Google expires the sign-in after seven days, and the workflow quietly stops writing.
Once it works, go back and publish the app.
For your own account, Google shows an unverified app warning you can click through, and the sign-in stops expiring.

params.show: Client ID + secret into the n8n credential → Sign in with Google. Then publish the app.

lines: Now add a Google Sheets node, rename it save lead, and choose the operation append or update row.
Pick your credential, then the Leads document, and the sheet, from the lists.

params.show: Google Sheets, renamed Save lead, Append or Update Row, Leads / Sheet1

lines: Set column to match on, to email.
That's what makes it append or update. A new email adds a row. An email we've seen before updates that row, instead of creating a duplicate.
Mapping is map each column manually, and because the names match, each field drags straight into its column.
Under options, set cell format to let Google Sheets format, so received at becomes a real date you can do maths with later.

params.show: Column to match on: email · Map Each Column Manually · Cell Format

notes.html: Options → Cell Format: Let Google Sheets format

lines: Execute the step, and switch to the sheet.
There's our test lead, in row two.

params.show: Execute step → switch to the sheet: row 2

lines: Next, the reply. Add a Gmail node, rename it reply to lead, and choose send.
Create a Gmail credential with the same client ID and secret, and sign in again.
This time Google asks for permission to send email.

params.show: Gmail, renamed Reply to lead, Send, new Gmail credential

lines: For to, don't use the incoming data directly.
After the sheet node, that data is the sheet's response, so reach back to the tidy node instead.
Dollar, open bracket, tidy lead, then item dot json dot email.
Subject, got your message, then the name. And email type, text.

params.show: To / Subject from Tidy lead · Email Type: Text

lines: The message is short and honest.
Thanks for getting in touch. Here's what happens next, and when you'll hear from a person.
And one question that makes your real reply better, like when they're hoping to start.
Then open the options and turn off append n8n attribution, or every reply ends with a line saying it was sent by n8n.

params.show: Message text · Options → Append n8n Attribution off

notes.html: What happens next · when a person replies

lines: Now your phone. In Telegram, open a chat with BotFather, and send slash new bot.
Give it a name, and a username ending in bot, and copy the token it gives you.
Treat that token like a password.

params.show: @BotFather → /newbot → name → username ending in bot → copy token

lines: Send your new bot any message, so it's allowed to message you back.
Then open this address in your browser, with your token in it, and find chat, then id.
That number is where your alerts will go.

params.show: Message the bot → open getUpdates → chat.id

lines: Back in n8n, add a Telegram node, rename it alert me, and choose send message.
Create the credential by pasting the token, and paste the chat ID.
Write the text. New lead, the name, what they need, their email and phone, and a link to the sheet.
Under additional fields, turn off append n8n attribution here too.
Execute the step, and the alert lands on your phone.

params.show: Telegram, renamed Alert me, Send Message, token credential, chat ID, text

lines: So that's the first half working.
Every lead is written down, answered within a minute, and on your phone.
Before we build the second half, two decisions that matter more than any node.
First, the status column. Who changes it from new to replied?
You do.
When you get back to a lead, you change their row.
It's the one manual step in the whole workflow, and it's on purpose, because it's the only honest record of whether a person actually got back to them.
Second, the reminder we're about to build goes to you, not the lead.
An automatic chaser to someone who hasn't answered is how a helpful business starts to look like a mailing list.
The workflow's job is to make sure a person follows up, not to do it for them.
Back to the canvas.

pills: The reminder goes to you, not the lead

lines: Add a wait node after alert me, and rename it wait until next working morning.
Set resume to at specified time, and switch the date and time field to an expression.

params.show: Wait, renamed, Resume: At Specified Time, Date and Time as an expression

chapter: Step 6: Wait for the next working morning

lines: The expression takes now, and adds one day.
Or, on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday, enough days to reach Monday.
Then it sets the time to nine o'clock. You can copy it from the description.

params.show: The next-working-morning expression

lines: That nine o'clock follows the workflow's time zone, so open the workflow settings and set it to yours.
On a self-hosted n8n, the default comes from your server's settings, and if nobody set it, n8n assumes New York time.

params.show: Settings → Timezone: yours

lines: When it wakes up, it needs to know what has happened since.
Add a Google Sheets node, rename it look up lead, and choose get rows, with the same document and sheet.
Add a filter. Column email, and the value is the email from tidy lead.

params.tag: STEP 7 · Google Sheets → Look up lead
params.show: Get Row(s), filter email = Tidy lead email

lines: Then an if node, called still new.
The condition is status, from the lookup, is equal to new, as a string.
If it's true, nobody has replied. If it's false, someone has, and that branch just ends.

params.show: If: status is equal to new

lines: On the true branch, add one more Telegram node, remind me, with the same chat.
The text says the name, that they've waited since received at, and that nobody has replied yet.

params.show: On the true branch: Telegram, same chat, reminder text

notes.html: Text: {{ name }} has waited since {{ received_at }}. Nobody has replied yet.

lines: Now the part most people skip.
Create a second workflow, called lead alarm.
Add an error trigger, and after it a Telegram node with the alarm text.
Which workflow failed, at which node, the error message, and a link to the execution. Then save it.

params.show: New workflow Lead alarm: Error Trigger → Telegram

lines: Go back to lead catcher, open its settings, and set error workflow to lead alarm.
One catch. Error workflows only run for live executions, not when you click execute in the editor.
We'll test it properly in a minute.

params.show: Lead catcher → Settings → Error workflow: Lead alarm

lines: Last step before the live run. Switch the workflow on.
Then open the form trigger, and copy the production URL, not the test one. The test URL only works while you're watching the editor.
And here's the second self-hosted catch.
If the production URL says localhost, set the webhook URL environment variable on your server to your real domain, and restart n8n, or nobody outside your server can reach the form.

params.show: Switch the workflow on · copy the Production URL · WEBHOOK_URL

lines: Right, let's run it for real.
For this demo, I've switched the wait node to after time interval, one minute, so we don't have to wait until tomorrow.
Open the production form, and submit a lead the way a customer would.

params.show: Production form → submit as a customer

notes.html: Demo only: Wait → After Time Interval · 1 minute

lines: The completion message shows straight away.
A few seconds later, the alert arrives on my phone.
In the inbox, the reply is already there, from my own address, with no n8n footer.
And in the sheet, a new row, with the status new.

params.show: Completion message → Telegram alert → inbox reply → new sheet row

lines: In executions, you can see this run, waiting.
After a minute, it wakes up, looks the lead up, finds the status still says new, and the reminder lands on my phone.

params.show: Executions: run Waiting → wakes → reminder arrives

lines: Now a second lead. This time, before the minute is up, I change the row's status to replied.
When the run wakes up, the if node takes the false branch, and nothing is sent.
That's the whole loop, working.

params.show: Second lead → set status to replied → run ends at If (false)

lines: Finally, let's break it on purpose.
In tidy lead, I misspell the name field in the expression, make the change live, and submit one more lead.
The step fails, and seconds later, lead alarm messages my phone, with the node and the error.
Put the spelling back, make it live again, and we're done.

params.tag: LIVE RUN · Break it on purpose
params.show: Typo in Tidy lead → submit → Lead alarm on the phone → fix

lines: Before you leave it running, set the wait node back to the next working morning, and make that change live.
Then once a week, fill in your own form. Thirty seconds.
If the reply and the alert both arrive, the whole chain works.

pills: Once a week: test your own form

lines: And when you reply to a lead, fill in replied at as well as the status.
After a few weeks, the gap between received at and replied at is your real response time, lead by lead.
It's usually longer than people guess, and it's the one number that tells you whether the leak is actually fixed.
None of this brings you a single new lead.
It stops you losing the ones that already chose you, which is the cheapest growth there is.
Every setting and expression from this build is in the description.
Build it tonight, then fill in your own form, and see how long it takes you to hear back.

pills: Keep the leads that already chose you
